text:
**Illegal Monday** 
The type of white paper that launched the account. Long post. Citations at end.

Why Tech Workers Fighting Visas Cannot Afford to Dismiss Illegal Immigration

Six arguments, one labor market, and the illegal labor that does not file an LCA

Chief Engineer | September 2026 | Evidence brief for intelligent followers. tl;dr can move along. Not a press release.

Abstract:
Tech workers have a clean target in the H-1B system because the government publishes the filings. That visibility is useful and incomplete. Unauthorized labor is larger, harder to count, and already inside industries that look corporate on a W-2. This brief lays out six reasons visa-focused workers should treat illegal immigration as a first-order problem: one labor market, housing and schools, shared document fraud, political headcount, the collapse of high-trust work, and a hidden office pipeline that never appears in lottery data. The strongest claim is the last one. Visas have a database. Illegal office labor has a stolen Social Security number and an I-9 a manager certified as genuine.

Introduction
H-1B is measurable. In fiscal year 2024, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services approved 399,395 H-1B petitions. Seventy-one percent of those beneficiaries were born in India (U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, 2025). Engineers can name the vendors, pull Labor Condition Applications, and argue about wages. Unauthorized presence does not come with that dashboard.

Pew Research Center estimated 14 million unauthorized immigrants in the United States in 2023, with 9.7 million in the workforce, 5.6 percent of all U.S. workers (Passel and Krogstad, 2025). Professional and business services, the industry bucket that includes staffing, contractors, and back-office work next to engineers, ran about 7 percent unauthorized in 2023 (Passel and Krogstad, 2025).
Treat that 14 million figure as real. At that scale the implication for American tech labor is horrific. No exaggeration.

Set aside agriculture and construction for a moment. Those still hurt tech workers. That is another post.
The six arguments below are not separate crusades. They are one system viewed from the desk of a worker who already knows the visa fight and has been told the other fight is someone else's problem.

Too many comments read: I don't care about illegals. That is ignorance on display.

Here is why.

The Six Arguments
The labor pool is one market

Visa fights decide who sits in the cube. Illegal hiring decides what the floor under that cube costs. Unauthorized workers were 15 percent of construction and 14 percent of agriculture in 2023, and 8 percent of leisure and hospitality (Passel and Krogstad, 2025). Those trades set local wages, housing starts, food prices, and logistics costs in the same metros that absorbed H-1B growth. Employers who can tap an unauthorized pool do not compete as hard for legal labor anywhere on the wage ladder. Calling the result a labor shortage is a slogan. It is a suppressed reservation wage. A tech worker who only audits the lottery is measuring the labeled pipe and ignoring the unlabeled one that still moves the cost of living.

Housing and schools are not a side issue

Nominal tech pay looks high until rent, property tax, classroom size, and emergency-room wait times eat it. Unauthorized households concentrate in the same states that already run large Indian and other visa populations: California, Texas, New Jersey, and similar hubs (Passel and Krogstad, 2025; Ward and Batalova, 2026). School districts enroll first and match immigration files later, if they match them at all. A B-2 visitor is not authorized to use public K-12 as a regular student under federal rules, yet local practice often treats presence as residency (Immigration and Nationality Act section 214(m)). Visa reform that leaves interior status unenforced does not save the school or the starter home. This rearranges who gets the scarce seat.

Status fraud is the same picture

Overstaying a tourist visa, working after a petition dies, using a stolen Social Security number, and sitting on a B-2 while relatives work are not a different moral category from H-1B abuse. They are the same failure: nobody matches the body to the file. Form I-9 requires the employer to examine documents and certify, under penalty of law, that they appear genuine and relate to the person (8 U.S.C. section 1324a). Repeated I-9 failure, identity theft on a payroll, and vendor layers that hide the worker are how both the staffing firm and the cash crew stay in business.

ICE worksite cases keep finding stolen numbers used for wages and benefits (U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, 2025; U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, 2026). If the shop is never reported, neither lane to these jobs gets cut.

Politics follows headcount, not job titles

Sanctuary rules, benefit access, driver's licenses, and census apportionment are driven by the large unauthorized population, not by the annual H-1B cap. Pew's 14 million figure for 2023, with about 6 million holding some temporary protection and about 8 million holding none, is a political mass (Passel and Krogstad, 2025). ICE manpower is finite. A force on the order of 22,000 agents cannot do worksite, street, and jail detainers at once. The cheap-labor lobby uses both the visa statute and the unenforced interior to exploit the resource for profit. Split the issue into "skilled good, illegal other" and the same donors keep E-Verify voluntary and interior enforcement thin. Tech workers still pay the coalition that protects both pipelines.

High-trust work dies when the surrounding county is low-trust

Engineering assumes contracts, credentials, and a common language in the meeting. A county that will not remove a known unauthorized crime family, or a hospital that staffs people who cannot communicate a consent, is not a county that stays good at intellectual property and quality control. Multi-generational American workers, including Hispanic families with roots older than living memory, are not the problem. The problem is a system that treats status as optional and undeserved while expecting the office to remain high-trust. You cannot run a specialty-occupation economy on I-9 theater and hope the schools, jails, and clinics stay someone else's responsibility.

The hidden corporate path for illegal employees is larger in uncertainty than the lottery

H-1B is apparent to us because Labor Condition Applications and petition counts are public. Unauthorized corporate labor does not file an LCA. It files an I-9 with a stolen number that belongs to a citizen, a child, or a dead account, or it keeps a badge after OPT or H-1B status expires. The Social Security Administration has long documented name-number mismatches and SSN misuse by noncitizens not authorized to work (Social Security Administration Office of the Inspector General, 2004). Later estimates put millions of unauthorized workers on valid or borrowed numbers in some years, with the Earnings Suspense File holding unmatched wages at enormous scale.

ICE's Glenn Valley Foods operation found about 70 illegal aliens using stolen identities and more than 100 citizen victims whose prescriptions, disability checks, taxes, and licenses were wrecked (U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, 2025). A Kentucky window plant produced indictments for stolen numbers on I-9s (U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, 2026). From the next desk that person looks like a coworker. From USCIS they are out of status. There is no public headcount of unauthorized workers in software, help desk, or vendor IT. That gap is the point. Absence of a lottery table is not absence of bodies.

The Strongest Argument**

The strongest argument is not that every engineer should stop caring about H-1B. The strongest argument is that H-1B is just one labeled slice of a substitution system made up of many others, and the unlabeled slice sits in the same buildings.

A lottery you can screenshot will always attract more heat than a stolen SSN on a W-2. That is a measurement error, not a conclusion about harm.

Most do not realize it, but these illegal aliens are in tech and management jobs. By the numbers which are certainly understated... millions of them- they just aren't filing their job or foreign college on a register that we can see but they are web developers, programmers, MBA, and scientists all the same. There is almost no occupation untaught in a foreign country that hasn't been found to be employed in the USA illegally. 

Professional and business services already carried a 7 percent unauthorized share in 2023 (Passel and Krogstad, 2025). Identity-theft worksite cases prove the method for getting onto formal payroll. Status rot (overstay, lapsed petition, B-2 plus remote work) proves the method for staying off the H-1B list while keeping the badge. Employers certify documents. Vendors hide the headcount. Citizens absorb the tax and credit damage when the number was stolen, with no voice to make it public. Tech workers who treat illegal presence as a blue-collar story are volunteering to miss the massive number of jobs that are theirs.

If the standard is "show me the LCA," the unauthorized office worker will always win the argument by disappearing. The correct standard is whether the person is authorized to work. That question belongs to ICE, USCIS, and the Department of Labor, and it only gets asked when someone reports what they saw.

Summation
What this brief established is simple. Visa abuse is real, documented, and concentrated. The visa system itself is abusive to our unemployed degreed labor. It attracts the majority of attention.

This is hard to accept but has to be understood.

Unauthorized presence is larger, less visible, and already inside industries that are not farms. One labor market means construction and hospitality wages still move the cost of living for engineers. Imagine if competition for employees pushed wages to 30 dollars per hour to match inflation. Where would an engineering salary lie? Document fraud and weak I-9s are all in the same bucket. 

Political power tracks bodies, not job codes, and they profit off the capital with Chamber of Commerce money greasing the cheap-labor transactions that sell out our prosperity.

High-trust work cannot be isolated from the country that refuses to enforce status. The hidden corporate pipeline is the piece visa activists are most likely to miss.

The practical implication is not to abandon H-1B reform. It is to stop treating interior enforcement as a lower-class errand. Report unauthorized hiring. Demand E-Verify with teeth. Treat overstay and stolen-identity payroll as illegal employment, because that is what the statute already says. The laws are there and we should push for enforcement of every single statute. The harm is generational and lowers the potential of our society through a cash-out dilution. A specialty-occupation workforce that only polices the lottery will keep losing to the underground illegal system that never files one.

References
8 U.S.C. section 1324a. Unlawful employment of aliens.
Immigration and Nationality Act section 214(m), 8 U.S.C. section 1184(m). Limitation on public school attendance for certain nonimmigrants.
Passel, J. S., and Krogstad, J. M. (2025, August 21). U.S. unauthorized immigrant population reached a record 14 million in 2023. Pew Research Center.
Social Security Administration, Office of the Inspector General. (2004). Social Security numbers: Noncitizens with earnings and unauthorized work (A-03-04-14037).
U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. (2025). Characteristics of H-1B specialty occupation workers: Fiscal year 2024 annual report to Congress.
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. (2025, June 18). ICE worksite enforcement operation uncovers widespread identity theft affecting more than 100 victims across the nation.
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. (2026, June 17). Fraud crackdown: 13 illegal aliens arrested, 8 indicted for using stolen Social Security numbers to work in Kentucky.
Ward, N., and Batalova, J. (2026). Indian immigrants in the United States. Migration Policy Institute.
Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. (2026). Advisory on financial activity associated with non-work-authorized populations.

This brief is for public discussion on Illegal Monday. It is not legal advice. Report suspected unauthorized employment to ICE (866-347-2423 or ) and suspected visa or petition fraud to USCIS.

Bookmark this. Share or quote it. Comment if you have watched an office treat illegal presence as someone else's problem. 

Follow for more Illegal Monday.

text:
This is not a meme.

This is a product-market fit case study, and it just made a quarter-million-dollar machine look overdesigned.

No funding round. No pitch deck. No roadmap. No "stakeholder alignment" meeting that ate three Tuesdays.

Just a problem, a pile of scrap, and a person too stubborn to wait for permission.

And it works.

That should make every engineer, founder and product manager in your timeline a little uncomfortable.

Here is why. This is a long one. Bookmark it now, because by the end you will never look at the word "technology" the same way again.

Let's start with the number that nobody in a procurement office likes to say out loud.

1. THE MATH THAT BREAKS THE ROOM

A new municipal street sweeper, the kind a city buys through a formal tender, commonly lands somewhere in the range of $150,000 to $300,000 depending on type and spec. Regenerative-air and vacuum models sit at the expensive end. Add the diesel, the trained operator, the maintenance contract, the spare parts pipeline, the depot, the insurance, the paperwork.

Now ask a rude question.

What percentage of that price is the actual act of moving dirt from the middle of a road to the side of a road?

Be honest. It is a small slice.

The rest is the cost of being an institution. Compliance. Warranty. Emissions standards. Safety certification. Procurement law. Brand. Sales commissions. Dealer margin. The cost of never being allowed to fail in public.

None of that is evil. Most of it exists for a reason.

But it creates a gap. A giant, expensive, invisible gap between "what the job physically requires" and "what the official solution costs."

And every single time there is a gap like that, somebody eventually walks into it with a welding torch.

That gap is where innovation actually lives. Not in the labs. Not in the keynote. In the gap.

2. A 177-YEAR-OLD SECRET

The mechanical street sweeper is not a modern idea. In 1849, an American inventor named Charles Brooks patented a rotating-brush sweeping machine pulled by horses. Before that, cities relied on people with brooms and, frankly, on rain.

Read that again.

The core mechanism, a brush that turns and pushes debris sideways as the vehicle moves, is older than the telephone, the light bulb and the modern bicycle.

Nearly two centuries later, the industry has added hydraulics, sensors, water sprays, dust suppression, GPS fleet tracking and touchscreens.

The principle did not change at all.

Which raises a question that should keep you up tonight:

If the principle is 177 years old and free to everyone, what exactly are you paying for?

Sometimes the answer is real. Reliability. Scale. Safety. Uptime across a fleet of five hundred machines.

And sometimes the answer is: a story you were told about why it has to be complicated.

3. WHAT "TECHNOLOGY" ACTUALLY MEANS

Somewhere along the way we let the word get hijacked.

Today "technology" means a screen. A chip. A subscription. A launch event with dramatic lighting and a founder in a black shirt.

But the original meaning is much older and much more honest:

Technology is a method for getting a result with less effort than before.

That is the whole definition. Less effort. Same result. Or better result.

Notice what is missing from it.

It does not say "expensive." It does not say "certified." It does not say "venture-backed." It does not say "approved by anyone."

By that definition, a machine assembled from spare parts that clears a road every day is not a joke about technology.

It is technology, in its purest form. Stripped of marketing. Stripped of ego. Stripped of the pitch.

The question is never "how impressive does it look?"

The question is always "how much work did it remove, and at what cost?"

Run that test on your own product. Run it on your company. Run it on your last six months.

Most of us will not enjoy the score.

4. THE WORD WEST SILICON VALLEY NEVER LEARNED TO PRONOUNCE

In India there is a word: jugaad.

It roughly means a clever, improvised fix made with whatever is available. Critics use it as an insult for sloppy work. Admirers use it as a badge of genius. Both are a little right.

Now look at what improvisation under constraint has actually produced.

In 1995, a Nigerian teacher named Mohammed Bah Abba built the pot-in-pot cooler: two clay pots, wet sand between them, evaporation doing the cooling. No electricity. It kept produce fresh for days longer in hot regions and earned him international recognition.

In 2002, a fourteen-year-old in Malawi named William Kamkwamba built a working windmill from scrap, bicycle parts and salvaged material to power lights in his family home during a famine. He learned the physics from library books he could barely read in English.

In 2007, Kenya's M-Pesa turned an ordinary basic mobile phone into a bank account for millions of people who had never touched a bank. No smartphone. No app store. Just text messages and a network of agents at corner shops.

Notice the pattern.

Nobody had the ideal materials.
Nobody had the ideal budget.
Nobody had the ideal infrastructure.

And every one of these solved a real problem for real people faster than a well-funded alternative did.

Constraint did not block the innovation.

Constraint was the innovation.

5. WHY SCARCITY MAKES BETTER ENGINEERS

Give a team unlimited budget and a blank sheet and watch what happens.

They add features.
They add layers.
They add dependencies.
They add a second dashboard for the first dashboard.

Give a single person one weekend, no budget and a pile of parts, and something completely different happens.

They ask the only question that matters: what is the least I can build that still does the job?

That question is a superpower. It forces you to find the actual core of the problem. It kills every feature that exists only to make you feel professional.

Scarcity is a filter. It removes vanity.

Here is the uncomfortable corollary for anyone building anything in 2026:

If you can only build something good when you have a big budget, you do not understand your problem yet.

The best test of understanding is being able to solve it badly, quickly, with junk.

If you can do that, you can then do it well. If you cannot, money will only hide the confusion for a while.

6. GALL'S LAW, OR WHY THE UGLY THING WINS

In 1975 a physician and systems theorist named John Gall wrote a book about why complex systems fail. It contains one line every builder should tattoo somewhere visible.

A complex system that works is invariably found to have evolved from a simple system that worked. A complex system designed from scratch never works and cannot be patched up to make it work. You have to start over with a working simple system.

Think about how many companies violate this every year.

They spend eighteen months building the perfect platform. They raise the round for the perfect platform. They hire forty people for the perfect platform.

Then they launch and discover that customers wanted a much smaller thing, and a competitor with a scrappy prototype has been eating their lunch since month three.

The ugly machine is not ugly because its builder lacked taste.

It is ugly because it went from idea to reality in days, and every day it existed it taught its builder something a whiteboard never could.

Reality is the best product manager alive. It is free, it is brutal and it never schedules a meeting.

Ship the thing that works badly. Then improve the thing that exists.

7. WORSE IS BETTER

In 1989 the computer scientist Richard Gabriel described a strange pattern in software. He called it "worse is better."

The idea: a simple, slightly incomplete solution that spreads quickly often beats a beautiful, complete solution that arrives late.

Unix beat more elegant systems this way. The early web beat far more sophisticated hypertext designs this way. A crude protocol that anyone could implement in a weekend conquered the world while the perfect alternatives were still in committee.

Why does this happen?

Because distribution beats perfection. Because simple things can be copied, fixed and extended by people who did not build them. Because a rough tool in the hands of a thousand users teaches more than a polished tool in the hands of ten.

A thing that is easy to understand is a thing that can be repaired.

A thing that can be repaired is a thing that survives.

Look at the machine that inspired this post one more time in your mind, and ask yourself which parts a stranger could fix on the side of a road with a wrench and twenty minutes.

Now ask the same about your product.

8. THE JUICERO PROBLEM

Remember Juicero?

A Silicon Valley startup raised well over one hundred million dollars to build a Wi-Fi-connected juicer. The machine retailed at hundreds of dollars and required proprietary juice packs.

Then journalists discovered that you could squeeze the packs with your bare hands and get roughly the same result.

The company shut down in 2017.

Here is the lesson. It was not that the engineering was bad. The engineering was extraordinary. The lesson is that nobody had asked the boring question first:

What is the simplest possible way to get juice out of a bag?

Put that story next to any improvised machine that quietly does its job every day for pennies, and one of them is a warning about the future and the other is a joke about the past.

Guess which one people laugh at.

That laugh is the most expensive habit in modern business.

9. THE HONEST COUNTERARGUMENT (BECAUSE I'M NOT SELLING YOU A FAIRY TALE)

Let me be fair, because the internet needs more of that.

A homemade rig is not a replacement for a professional fleet. Not always. Not even often.

Standards exist because people got hurt. Certification exists because bridges fell and boilers exploded. Warranties exist because "it worked on my machine" is not a service level agreement.

A crude device can be dangerous to its operator. It can fail without warning. It cannot be scaled to a city of two million people. It has no documentation, no spare parts pipeline and no one to call at 3 a.m.

So no, the lesson is not "throw away the rulebook."

The lesson is much sharper:

Professional solutions must justify every dollar above the crude baseline.

Every feature. Every layer. Every line of the spec. If you cannot explain what it buys the customer, you are not building quality.

You are building comfort. Your own.

The improvised machine is a baseline, a benchmark, an audit. It tells you the floor of what the job actually costs. Everything above that floor had better be worth it.

Most organizations never run that audit, because they never look at the floor.

10. THE THREE KINDS OF BUILDERS

After more than a decade around products, teams and platforms, I see exactly three types of people.

The first type waits.

They wait for budget, for approval, for the right tools, for the reorg to finish, for the roadmap to open a slot. They are often smart. They are very often right about why it cannot be done. They produce beautiful reasons.

The second type plans.

They write the strategy, draw the architecture, run the workshops, align the stakeholders. Some of them ship something excellent. Many ship it a year late to a market that moved on.

The third type builds.

They look at what is lying around, look at the problem, and start connecting the two. Their first version embarrasses them. Their fifth version embarrasses their competitors.

The third type is rare. Not because it takes genius. Because it takes a specific kind of courage: the willingness to be seen making something imperfect in public.

That is the actual scarce resource in any industry. Not capital. Not talent. Not ideas.

Willingness to look a little ridiculous while it works.

11. THE HIDDEN SKILL: SEEING WHAT IS LYING AROUND

The French anthropologist Claude Levi-Strauss used a word for this: bricolage. Working with whatever is at hand and repurposing it for a new job.

The bricoleur does not begin with a perfect plan and order the perfect parts.

The bricoleur begins by looking at the parts.

That inversion is enormous.

Most corporate innovation starts with a goal and then shops for solutions. Bricolage starts with an inventory and then discovers goals.

Why does that matter? Because the parts are real, cheap and available today. The perfect plan is imaginary and always six months away.

Every major technology shift had this flavor.

Early personal computers were hobbyist machines built from parts. The first Google servers famously used cheap commodity hardware instead of expensive enterprise gear, and the software was designed to survive the hardware dying. The first successful private rockets were built by people who refused to accept that launch had to cost what governments said it cost.

The winning move was never "buy the best."

It was "understand the job so well that the cheap thing can do it."

12. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE AI ERA

Now the part that should actually change your next quarter.

We are living through the biggest collapse in the cost of building software in history. Tasks that needed a team and a budget two years ago now need one person and an afternoon.

Which means the gap from earlier is opening everywhere at once.

Every overpriced SaaS tool, every bloated internal system, every enterprise product that survives on switching costs and sales dinners is now sitting in a gap between "what the job requires" and "what it costs."

And there are millions of people with a welding torch.

They are not waiting for permission. They are not attending your webinar. They are stringing together models, APIs, spreadsheets and scripts into crude machines that do one job well.

They look embarrassing. Their demos have bugs. Their interfaces would make a designer cry.

They also solve the problem for one hundredth of the price.

If your business model depends on the customer not noticing how simple the core job is, you are running on borrowed time. The borrowing rate just went up.

The winners of this era will not be the ones with the most sophisticated stack.

They will be the ones who understand the problem so cleanly that they can solve it with almost nothing, and then know exactly where to add sophistication that a customer would happily pay for.

13. THE ELEGANCE TRAP

Here is a trap that catches the most talented people I know.

They mistake elegance for value.

Elegance is a feeling inside the builder. Value is a result inside the customer. The two overlap sometimes. Not always.

I have watched brilliant engineers spend six weeks making a system beautiful that nobody had asked for, while a crude script written in an hour was quietly running the entire process.

I have watched design teams polish an onboarding flow to perfection for a product with no users.

I have watched founders refuse to launch because the logo was not ready.

The world does not pay for elegance. It pays for problems removed.

Sometimes elegance removes problems. Sometimes it is just an expensive way to feel like a professional.

Here is a simple diagnostic:

If your customer saw everything behind the curtain, would they be impressed or would they be annoyed at what they paid for?

The honest answer tells you where to cut.

14. THE 12 RULES OF THE UGLY MACHINE

You have read this far, so here is the practical part. Twelve rules stolen from every improvised device that has ever quietly beaten a professional one.

Rule 1. Define the job in one sentence. If you need two, you have two jobs and two products.

Rule 2. Find the cheapest thing that could possibly do it. Not the best. The cheapest. Then find out how it fails.

Rule 3. Use what is lying around before you buy anything. Inventory first, shopping second.

Rule 4. Make the first version in a day, not a quarter. If it takes longer, you are building the wrong first version.

Rule 5. Put it in front of the real problem immediately. A prototype that has never touched reality is a hypothesis wearing a costume.

Rule 6. Make it repairable by a stranger. Complexity that only its creator understands is a liability, not an asset.

Rule 7. Every added part must earn its place. Ask what breaks if you remove it. If the answer is "nothing," remove it.

Rule 8. Watch where it fails, not where it succeeds. Failure is the only honest feedback you will get for free.

Rule 9. Upgrade the bottleneck only. Do not touch the parts that already work. Polish is a tax on everything you did not need to polish.

Rule 10. Keep the cost of one attempt lower than the cost of one meeting. Then you can afford to be wrong a hundred times.

Rule 11. Do not apologize for the ugliness. Explain the result. Nobody remembers the paint.

Rule 12. Stay a builder after you become successful. The moment you start only reviewing, someone with a welding torch has started building your replacement.

15. WHY THE LAUGH IS THE WARNING

Let's talk about the reaction.

When people see something improvised and effective, the first response is often a laugh. A smirk. A "haha, only there."

Pay attention to that laugh. It is not neutral.

It is a defense mechanism. It is how a comfortable system protects itself from a question it does not want to answer.

The laugh says: that is not real technology.

Fine. Then define it.

If real technology means a solution to a problem, then this counts.
If real technology means a solution that scales, we can debate that.
If real technology means a solution that looks impressive, then congratulations, you have defined it as theater.

Every era has this reaction.

The first personal computers were toys. The first web pages were toys. The first smartphone apps were toys. The first electric cars were golf carts. The first reusable rockets were an expensive stunt.

The pattern is remarkably consistent:

First they laugh at how crude it looks.
Then they ask how it works.
Then they ask how much it costs.
Then they ask why they did not build it.

The laugh always comes first. It is the earliest sign that something has gone right.

16. THE SPEC SHEET NOBODY READS

Every product has two price tags.

The first is on the box. The second is hidden inside the customer's life: the time to learn it, the time to fix it, the time to wait for someone who is allowed to fix it, the time to migrate away when it stops fitting.

Improvised solutions almost always win on the second tag.

The person who built the thing understands it completely. There is no support queue. There is no "please upgrade to the enterprise plan to unlock this feature." There is no vendor roadmap to pray over.

When it breaks, the fix is a conversation between one person and one problem.

Compare that to how most of us live with our tools. We rent software we do not understand, run on servers we cannot see, under terms we did not read, and call it "modern."

We have traded ownership for convenience so gradually that we forgot it was a trade.

There is a quiet power in owning the whole machine, even a rough one. You know what every part does. You know why it is there. You can change it tonight.

That power is worth more than most feature lists admit.

It is also why the best builders keep at least one tool in their life that they made themselves, no matter how successful they become.

It keeps them honest about how much of the job is real and how much is packaging.

17. THE MACHINE YOU ARE NOT BUILDING

Now turn the camera around.

Somewhere in your life there is a road that needs clearing. A workflow that eats hours. A process everyone hates. A problem that has been "on the roadmap" for two years.

You know exactly which one.

And you have been telling yourself the same story: we need the right tool, the right budget, the right team, the right moment.

You do not.

You need one ugly version that works by Friday.

Not a plan for it. Not a deck about it. Not a doc titled "Vision for the future of X."

The thing itself. Held together with whatever you have. Embarrassing to show. Useful on day one.

The gap between you and that machine is not talent. It is not money. It is one decision: to start before you feel ready.

Every person you admire for building something remarkable started with a version they were ashamed of.

The only difference between them and everyone else is that they let the world see it anyway.

18. THE PREDICTION

Here is what I think happens over the next few years, and you can quote me when I am wrong.

The cost of building will keep collapsing. The cost of knowing what to build will not.

That means the scarce skill flips. Execution becomes cheap. Judgment becomes expensive.

The person who can look at a messy problem and say "the real job is this one small thing" will beat ten teams who can build anything but do not know what matters.

The improvised machine is a preview of that world. Its builder did not need a bigger budget. Its builder needed a sharper understanding of the job.

Expect more of this, everywhere, in every industry.

Expect tools that look silly and work brilliantly.
Expect companies that look tiny and serve millions.
Expect products that break every rule of "professional" and still win, because the customer never cared about the rules. The customer cared about the result.

And expect a lot of very well-funded organizations to be genuinely confused about how this happened.

It will not be a mystery. It will be a gap, and someone will have walked into it.

19. THE QUESTION TO CARRY OUT OF HERE

Strip everything away.

Forget the tech stack. Forget the org chart. Forget the industry.

There is one question underneath all of it, and the whole post is just a long way of asking it:

What is the simplest thing that could possibly work?

Ask it about your product.
Ask it about your job.
Ask it about the project you have been stuck on since spring.
Ask it about the thing you keep calling "complicated."

Then, and this is the hard part, believe the answer.

Because the answer is almost always smaller, cheaper and sooner than you were hoping. And it is almost always available today.

The people who win are not the ones who found a smarter answer.

They are the ones who stopped hiding behind a bigger question.

The next time you see something improvised, effective and slightly ridiculous, do not laugh.

Take notes.

Somebody just showed you the floor of what the job costs, and everything you build above it has to be worth the price.

20. ONE LAST THING

Somewhere right now, a person is looking at a problem that a whole industry says costs a fortune to solve.

They do not have the fortune. They have a weekend, a pile of parts and a stubborn streak.

Most of the time nobody will ever write about what they build. There will be no launch, no funding announcement, no applause.

It will simply work, every day, for years, in a place you will never visit.

That is what technology looks like when nobody is watching: less a product than a decision, made by one person, to stop waiting.

The industry will keep selling the story that the job is complicated.

The floor keeps telling a different story.

Learn to hear it.

Before you scroll on, do one thing for me.

Pick the project you have been circling for months. Write down the job in a single sentence. Then write down the crudest possible way to get it done this week, using only what you already own.

Not the good way. Not the scalable way. The crude way.

Do that today, and you will learn more in 90 minutes than the last quarter of planning taught you.

Then come back and tell me what happened.

Small warning: it will feel silly. The result will look nothing like the version in your head. That feeling is not a sign you are doing it wrong. It is proof you have really started.

If this changed how you think about building, repost the first line so a builder you know can find it. Follow for more breakdowns like this, and tell me in the replies: what is the ugliest thing you ever built that actually worked?

text:
How to Read Iran's 26-Page Midterm Letter to American Voters in 10 Minutes

Iran picked a side in November. The same regime that named America the Great Satan spent 26 pages asking you to change who runs Congress, and it did not pick Republicans.

On Tuesday, September 29, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps published "An Open Letter to the Honorable People of the United States of America." Twenty-five pages or twenty-six, depending on who did the counting. Either way, that is longer than most of my students' research papers. And better formatted, frankly, which hurts.

The IRGC, for anyone keeping score at home, is the outfit President Trump designated a Foreign Terrorist Organization in 2019. It is now giving civics lessons to Ohio.

What is next, a terrorist army writing campaign literature for an American election... oh. Wait. I was just handed a note. They already did that.

I teach science, so we will do this the way I grade a lab report. Claim. Evidence. Conclusion. But first I owe you something, because I cannot read this letter the way a pundit reads it. I read it as a man Iran has already tried to kill.

— WHY THIS ONE IS PERSONAL —

I was an Army medic in Iraq.

Iran's militias blew up my vehicle while I was sitting in it. And they hurt my gunner.

I am going to say that again, slower, because I need the IRGC's English-language PR department to understand it. They. Hurt. My. Gunner.

If you have never ridden in a turret-topped truck, here is what you need to know. The gunner is the one standing up. Half of his body is out in the open so the rest of us can sit down behind armor. He is the first set of eyes, the first one exposed, and when something goes wrong he is the first one it finds. Every medic in every convoy knows exactly where his gunner is at every second. You do not lose track of your gunner. Ever.

So when I hear a regime spokesman say there is not "a single verifiable instance" of the IRGC hurting anyone, I do not need a fact-checker. I need a minute. And maybe a walk around the block.

The State Department has stated that Iran was responsible for the deaths of at least 603 American service members in Iraq between 2003 and 2011, mostly through militias it trained, funded, and handed explosively formed penetrators. An EFP is a copper plate that turns into a molten slug and punches through armor like it is wet cardboard. I know what one does to a truck. I know what it does to the men inside. I did not learn it from a documentary.

And now that same regime wants to tell me how to vote.

No one hurts my gunner. Nobody. And they sure as heck do not get a vote in my country afterward.

— WHAT THE LETTER ACTUALLY SAYS —

Alright. Deep breath. Back to the lab report.

To be fair, and I am always fair, the letter never prints the letter D. It does not have to.

It tells Americans that politicians win votes through "deception and false promises, as Trump did," and that we can "change the makeup of the government" by choosing differently. It calls the President a tyrant. It claims Iran won the war. (Bold strategy, considering the last seven months.) It wants American support for Israel ended and our overseas bases closed. Then it offers "peaceful coexistence."

And then, in the same document, it warns that people around the world will set fire to American interests and assets if we do not change course.

Coexistence. With a lit match in the other hand. It reads less like a peace offer and more like a breakup text from a stalker. "I just want what's best for you. Also, I know where you park."

Now, the part that matters for your ballot. President Trump is not on it this November. The only way to "change the makeup of the government" in 2026 is to change who controls the House and the Senate. There are two parties on that ballot.

The IRGC can count to two. So can you.

Jonathan Turley put it about as well as anyone could: it is not a good sign when the IRGC shifts from "Death to America" to "Vote Democratic."

— "WHY IS NOBODY REPORTING THIS?" —

Precision matters in this classroom, so here it is. Some outlets did. Reuters ran it. The New York Post ran it. The State Department answered it on Wednesday and called it a desperate smokescreen.

So let me ask the better question. How many minutes did your favorite evening newscast give it?

A designated terrorist organization publicly asking Americans to remove one party from power, five weeks before a federal election. If the Kremlin had mailed voters a 26-page letter begging them to vote Republican, we would know the font. We would know the paper weight. Rachel Maddow would have a corkboard and red string by Thursday.

Quinn's Law Number 2: If you want to know what liberals are up to, pay attention to what they accuse conservatives of doing. We spent years being told that a foreign power picking a side in an American election was a five-alarm emergency. It still is. It just gets a lot less interesting when the foreign power picks the "right" side.

— THIS IS NOT IRAN'S FIRST ELECTION —

The letter is new. The strategy is not.

o August 2020: the National Intelligence Council assessed that Iran was running an influence campaign to undermine the President and divide the country, and that Khamenei probably authorized it.

o 2024: the FBI and ODNI confirmed Iranian hackers broke into the Trump campaign, then sent the stolen material to people tied to the Biden campaign.

o November 2024: the Justice Department charged an IRGC-linked plot to assassinate Donald Trump.

Three straight cycles. Hack the man's campaign. Plot to kill the man. Then write 26 pages asking you to strip his party of power. If that is a coincidence, it is the most consistent coincidence in the history of statistics, and I grade lab reports from teenagers who think a sample size of one is "basically proof."

— "DEATH TO AMERICA" IS JUST A FIGURE OF SPEECH —

The letter insists the chant does not express any ill will toward the American people. It is aimed at our government. Not us. Never us.

Wonderful. Very reassuring. Tell it to my gunner.

Tell it to the families of the 241 Americans killed in their Beirut barracks in 1983 by a truck bomb driven by Hezbollah, the militia Iran built from scratch. A U.S. federal court later held Iran liable.

And the Iranian people would like a word about that "we never hurt civilians" line, too. Ask the family of Mahsa Amini, the 22-year-old who died in the custody of the morality police in 2022 because of how she wore her hijab. Ask the protesters shot in the street for wanting the exact freedoms the American left gives speeches about.

"Death to America" does not mean death to Americans. Got it. And "the dog ate my homework" means the dog is a literary critic.

— A MAN WHO WAS THERE IN 1979 —

If you want to understand who is writing you letters, skip cable news. Read V.S. Naipaul.

Naipaul won a Nobel Prize in Literature, traveled through Iran right after the 1979 revolution, and wrote Among the Believers: An Islamic Journey (1981). He was no conservative culture warrior. He was a skeptical, cranky, brilliant observer who could smell a fraud from across a courtyard. What he saw should keep you up at night.

He sat down with Ayatollah Khalkhali, the revolution's "hanging judge," who was openly pleased with himself over the executions he had ordered, the Shah's former prime minister among them.

He met a young man in Malaysia who praised Khomeini as a good man. Naipaul asked why. The only reason the young man could give was that Khomeini had banned women from appearing on television. That was the whole résumé. That was enough.

Naipaul described a faith turned into a sealed political community, where everything outside it was "impious, impure, infidel." His verdict after months on the ground was that the revolutionary faith could whip up a crowd, but it could not teach anyone how to run a modern state.

Forty-five years later, the state he watched being born is still running on fury instead of competence. Still exporting it. And now it would like to help you pick your Congress.

— FIGHT OR MADRID —

There are basically two ways a free people can answer terror.

One is United Flight 93, September 11, 2001. Passengers who had never met each other found out what the hijackers planned, took a vote, and rushed the cockpit. They died in a field in Pennsylvania, and the Capitol is still standing because of them. Nobody formed a committee. Nobody wrote a strongly worded letter. They fought.

The other is Madrid, March 2004. Terrorists bombed the commuter trains and killed nearly 200 people days before a national election. The voters changed the government, and the new government pulled Spain's troops out of Iraq. The terrorists learned exactly the lesson they hoped to learn. Bombs work. Elections can be bought with them.

The IRGC letter is a polite request for Madrid. It asks you to vote for surrender and call it peace.

Quinn's Law Number 15: To a liberal, every culture is unquestionable and of equal value, except the West's. That is how you end up with college-educated Americans, bless their hearts, nodding along to a "peaceful coexistence" offer from people who chant for their death on a weekly schedule. Some folks are one fry short of a Happy Meal. Some are missing the whole bag.

— THE GREAT SATAN AND THE LITTLE SATAN —

One more correction for the record, because I have heard this one get mangled.

Khomeini did not call America the second-worst devil. He called us the GREAT Satan. Israel only got "Little Satan." In the regime's own theology, we outrank the Jewish state on the list of things to destroy.

So the next time someone tells you this whole war is "really about Israel," gently remind them that Tehran's own ranking system puts YOU in first place. Congratulations. Nobody asked for the trophy.

And when the regime that ranks you above Israel on its enemies list writes 26 pages about whom you should support in November, the conclusion does not require a PhD. It requires a pulse.

— THE ONE QUESTION —

Every Democrat running in November should be asked one question, on camera: Do you reject the IRGC's support?

That is it. One question. It costs nothing to say yes. It is the easiest layup in American politics.

Keep track of who answers it plainly, and who pivots to "well, both sides." The pivot is the answer.

And to every voter reading this: you do not have to love your Republican candidate. I have said it before. In November you are hiring a vote, not a best friend. But if a foreign terrorist army has written you a letter explaining which way it would like you to vote... maybe do the other thing.

My gunner would tell you the same. He has the scars to back it up.

IF THIS ARTICLE MADE YOU THINK: LIKE this article so the algorithm shows it to people who need to read it. SHARE this. Every share really helps get the word out. Use it. COMMENT below with your take. Has your local news even mentioned the IRGC letter? Tell me.

And if you want MORE of this, the data, the history, the science, the stories, JOIN Bski's Classroom community or follow me on YouTube. Even better, subscribe to my account; it is about the cost of a cup of coffee per month. That is it. Your support keeps this classroom open, and I promise I will never run out of material as long as the left keeps trying to out-dumb itself.

But what do I know. I am only a medic who got blown up by Iran's militias once already, and I am not about to let them pick my Congress too.
@TPUSA @TPAction @JoJoFromJerz

Breaking :

EU Council wants to abolish correspondence secrecy

The EU member states want to abolish the modern secrecy of letters. In  the EU Council, the police should be able to prosecute private chat  flows and monitor such a letter communication. Experts warn that Signal  and WhatsApp could leave the EU.

The EU of citizens' rights – has this combination of words already  been heard? But the EU of governments, which is well there. The  elections in Belgium were held in parallel with the EU elections on 9.  held in June and ended with a triumph for the Flemish right-wing  conservatives (N-VA) and the Vlaams Belang. Liberal Prime Minister  Alexander De Croo immediately declared his resignation, but remains in  office. Its centre-left coalition will probably not be once again after  the losses suffered.

But now the country could end up one last coup in EU Brussels. Until  the 1. The Belgian Government holds the semi-annual Presidency of the EU  Council in July. Since the beginning of the year, the De Croo  government has been trying to enforce general chat control in the EU,  especially at end-to-end encrypted services such as WhatsApp or Signal.  EU bodies have been planning this advance for a long time. So far, there  have been one or two vetoos too much in the Council. But now France had  itself break out of the blocking minority. And so the Belgian proposal  could already be adopted in the Council on Wednesday.

The Regulation includes the title of "Rules to combat child abuse".  It is supposedly about images that record child abuse (child sexual  abuse material, CSAM), and also sent internet links should be scanned  automatically. Ultimately, it is about access to the online  communication of citizens. The laudable fight against child pornography  is the giant hammer, with which the small nail data protection and the  right to privacy for all citizens are to be sunk into the ground.
An increase in security is not expected

“Send me a Whatsapp,” you hear (still) everywhere. Many citizens use  the chat apps every day, almost self-evident, of course, also send a  picture, a meme, an Internet link. Three quarters of 16- to 74 year olds  across the EU are registered with one of the various apps such as  Skype, Telegram, Threema, etc. In Germany, 60 million alone use the  WhatsApp chat service, which has been part of the Facebook Group Meta  for some time. Since that is the case, many have been looking for  alternatives because Facebook is considered a data vacuum cleaner with  partly dubary terms of use. Now the EU wants to put it equally on the  Big Tech Group and gain insight into the private communication of the  citizens, block it or prosecute it in the event of a case. The country  bloc seizes the technical services and becomes the imitator of the large  tech companies, which it should actually include in the sense of the  freedom of its citizens.

If the EU regulation comes, app users will probably see one of these  windows at some point. In it, they are asked whether they agree to  verify their sent images, photos and videos by artificial intelligence  (AI) or not. If not, they will no longer be able to use the service or  at least not send any pictures, etc. However, it is likely that many  will agree with the new terms of use almost otherwise – and so the EU  would come a little closer to the comprehensive control of its citizens.

Those who have something to hide will simply not agree to the new  conditions and use darker channels, as they do today. So there would be  no increase in security for small children who fall victim to sexual  abuse and whose images are then spread. Ultimately, the EU regulation  amounts to suspend mass surveillance of citizens and thus possible  prosecution even where there is no plaintiff. For example, where  teenagers send lewd pictures. And AI can, of course, become erred and  possibly classify harmless content as potentially dangerous.
Legal service of the Council: Arbitrary control violates fundamental rights

Initially, even the checking of the chat messages and recorded voice  messages was planned on keywords. These are individual regulations that  were withdrawn for the first, according to the former MEP Patrick Breyer  (Pirates). In addition, France has returned a derogation for security  authorities and military, which can then continue to send pictures and  videos without these being subjected to any kind of scanning.

The Legal Service of the Council was still in force on 24. May found  that "arbitrary chat control" is still on the EU agenda for persons who  are not suspected of committing a crime and, of course, constitute a  violation of fundamental rights (in Germany Article 13 of the Basic  Law).

If the regulation comes, private chat providers can no longer keep  one of their most important promises. Signal’s president, Meredith  Whittaker, writes in a recent press release that “upload moderation” is  only a new word for mass chat control: “There is no way to implement  such proposals related to end-to-end encrypted communication without  fundamentally undermining encryption and creating a dangerous weakness  in a core infrastructure that would have a global impact far beyond  Europe.”

The claim that content is still being “checked before” its encryption  is contrary to the end-to-end principle with which WhatsApp and signal  promote itself. Signal had once developed open source technology,  WhatsApp took it over, Mark Zuckerberg has not yet touched it. According  to Whittaker, encryption and “upload moderation” do not go together –  this is an “mathematical reality” that new words could not hide either.  The EU chat control proposal is about “mass scanning” about “the same  old monitoring with a new label” using “mass scanning”.

One thing goes without saying that if the chat services were to know  about “illegal activities” due to the surveillance of image content and  Internet addresses, they would not only have to inform the EU state or  supranational authorities immediately about it, but also “act quickly to  remove or block access to access it”. The AI-supported detection of  supposedly illegal content would therefore also result in its deletion.
Whittaker: We are previously leaving the EU market

Already in May, Whittaker announced that he would rely on the EU  market rather than engage in an undermining of encryption technology.  Now Signal has remained a niche provider with 40 million users  worldwide.

In addition to the head of the Signal, the Society for Freedom Rights also protest the organisation European Digital Rights (entitled “Be scanned – or get banned!”) and the Center for Democracy & Technology (CDT) Europe strongly against the draft regulation of the Belgian Presidency.

However, even the industry giant WhatsApp recently threatened with  its retirement from India within 60 days, according to the trade  magazines Rest of World and Inside Digital.  The government had previously adopted a regulation requiring  significant services (those with more than five million users) to  disclose the first author of information. With half a billion users in  India, WhatsApp belongs to this category, similar to what is a “very  large platform” under the EU’s Digital Services Act (DSA) and is  therefore subject to EU censorship law. Due to the importance of  WhatsApp for the Indian economy, a compromise is expected.

In the EU, Germany, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Austria and Poland  have been against the plans. Now the Belgians were apparently able to  capture France through the concession for security services and the  military. The blocking minority in the Council could therefore tip this  Wednesday. It is frightening that the conditions in the EU Council have  become so scarce that a majority is tangible. Estonia, Finland, Greece,  Italy, Portugal, Sweden, Slovenia and the Czech Republic have not yet  determined.

The European Parliament in Strasbourg-Brussels spoke out in November  to maintain chat encryption. If the Council decision is taken on  Wednesday, then perhaps the hour of this Parliament could really beat:  it would then have to do everything possible to prevent chat control in  the so-called 'trilogue' of the three EU institutions.

text:
Statement: IFF condemns the internet shutdown in Connaught Place ahead of today's protest. We are tracing the suspension order.

New Delhi, 2 October 2026

The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) condemns the suspension of mobile internet services in and around Connaught Place, New Delhi, this morning. At 9:40 am, Jio subscribers in the area received a message stating: "As per government instructions Internet services have been stopped in your area till further notice." The shutdown took effect before a protest called for 11 am at Jantar Mantar, seeking the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, had even begun. 

Delhi Police has refused permission for the gathering, prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 are in force across New Delhi district, and entry and exit at eleven metro stations have been closed. On Gandhi Jayanti, the answer to a call for protest in the capital has been to switch off the internet for everyone who lives, works, trades and reports in its centre. We call for the immediate restoration of services. 

At the time of release of this statement, we have not been able to locate any suspension order published by the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Department of Telecommunications, the Government of NCT of Delhi or the Delhi Police. The public does not know who directed this shutdown, on what grounds, over what area, or until when. IFF is attempting to trace the order and will make it public as soon as we obtain a copy.

In Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India, (2020) 3 SCC 637, the Supreme Court held that speech and trade over the internet are protected under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g) of the Constitution, and that every suspension order must be published, reasoned, proportionate and limited in time. Under Section 20(2)(b) of the Telecommunications Act, 2023 and the Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules, 2024, only the Union or State Home Secretary may issue such an order, for reasons recorded in writing. The order must be published and must specify the area, the services and a fixed duration and it may be passed only where no other reasonable means would serve. A shutdown announced to subscribers as lasting "till further notice", imposed before a single person had assembled, cannot be squared with these safeguards. It follows repeated suspensions around Jantar Mantar in July 2026. Switching off the network is becoming a routine response to protest in the national capital. IFF condemns the internet shutdown in parts of Central Delhi. 

We call upon the Government of India and the Government of NCT of Delhi to:

1. Immediately restore mobile internet services in Connaught Place and all affected parts of Central Delhi.

2. Publish the suspension order forthwith, together with the reasons recorded in writing.

3. Disclose the issuing authority, the precise areas and services covered, and the period of operation.

4. Place the order before the Review Committee within five days, as the Rules require, and make its findings public.

text:
Five Arrested Near RAF Fairford After Suspicious Vans Stopped In UK

Five men were arrested early Sunday near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire after police received a report around 12:45am about three suspicious vans heading toward the air base.

Armed officers detained the men in nearby Whelford on suspicion of Explosives Act offences; they later also faced suspicion of preparing a terrorist act and remain in custody.

Counter-terrorism police now lead the inquiry, with support from MI5.

About 85 households were evacuated as a precaution and directed to a leisure centre.

The Army’s bomb disposal team is examining the vans inside a 400-metre cordon, using a robot.

Police say the incident is contained, with no explosion or injuries reported.

The operation was not planned in advance and began after a resident called police.

RAF Fairford hosts U.S. bombers used in recent operations against Iran, and U.S. personnel at the base say they remain vigilant.

Officials have not confirmed the vans were aimed at the base.

DCP Akanksha Yadav says, "On August 1, we received a complaint from a person who alleged that they had been duped in a visa fraud. Dear Sir/Madam,

I am Abhay Kumar Choudhary, S/o Shri Narayana Choudhary, resident of Banmankhi, Purnia, Bihar – 854202.

I had taken a Mudra Loan of ₹6,00,000 in the name of Gita Agency from State Bank of India (SBI), Banmankhi Branch, Purnia, Bihar – Branch Code 2910. I had been regularly paying the loan interest/EMI of approximately ₹6,000 per month. However, after the COVID-19 pandemic, my business suffered significant financial losses, due to which I was unable to continue making the payments on time.

On 10 December 2025, I received a notice and was asked to appear before the Lok Adalat. However, I did not receive a proper opportunity to present my case or explain my financial circumstances.

Subsequently, the Branch Manager, Ms. Parvati Singh, provided me with a settlement letter for an amount of approximately ₹2,50,000. I requested some additional time to arrange the settlement amount. Thereafter, I deposited ₹40,000 towards the loan and again requested reasonable time to arrange the remaining amount.

Unfortunately, instead of providing me reasonable time to resolve the matter, I have allegedly been subjected to repeated harassment, intimidation and threats. I was also threatened through police intervention and was allegedly told to commit suicide. I was further threatened with being sent to jail and other serious consequences.

I have an audio recording of the conversation containing the alleged threats and abusive/harassing statements, which I am attaching with this complaint as supporting evidence.

I fully understand my responsibility towards repayment of the loan and have already deposited ₹40,000 after the settlement discussion. I am willing to cooperate with the bank and repay/settle the outstanding dues as per applicable rules. However, I strongly object to any form of harassment, intimidation, abusive language, threats, or coercive recovery practices.

I therefore respectfully request the Reserve Bank of India to:

5. Provide me a fair opportunity to discuss and resolve the outstanding loan amount through a lawful settlement/restructuring mechanism, if applicable.

I am not refusing repayment of my loan. I am requesting a reasonable opportunity to resolve my financial liability lawfully and peacefully. I request RBI to kindly look into this matter urgently, considering the seriousness of the alleged threats and harassment.

I am attaching the available supporting documents, including the settlement letter, payment proof of ₹40,000, notices, and the audio recording of the alleged threatening conversation.

Kindly acknowledge my complaint and inform me about the appropriate action taken in this matter.

Thank you.

text:
Assi (#Assi #TaapseePannu #Revathy #SexualCrimes) - A gang abducts and rapes a woman who has a husband, a child, and a job, and then throws her onto a railway track. There are five perpetrators, but the police register only four. The medical report states that none of the accused persons’ DNA samples matched. Judge Vasudha orders a fresh medical report, yet once again, the DNA results do not match. The accused are granted bail. While the victim, Parima, struggles on one side just to cope with her daily life, on the other side, a group that believes money can buy anything suppresses the crime, secures bail for the accused, and gets them released. In such a situation, how the lawyer Raavi, who appears on behalf of the victim Parima in this case, fights to prove the truth, whether she identifies the real culprits and ensures punishment for them, and whether Parima receives justice, that forms the rest of the story.

The truth is that sexual crimes against women continue as an ongoing saga across India. Many times, they do not come to light, many times, they are covered up. Every day, news keeps emerging that women of various ages have been subjected to sexual assault by young men and even minors. But how does this news reach us? As a small boxed item. Media organizations that spend two full pages on political advertisements print such news in a tiny corner, almost unreadable to the public, like a brief boxed report. Proving crimes has also become increasingly difficult these days. Even in Tamil Nadu, we have seen in a case involving the sexual assault of a 10 year old girl that the police investigation officer threatened the child and subjected her to harsh questioning, and the audio of that incident was released. I too received a notice for posting that audio on social media, and that too on the very next day after the court ordered the case to be transferred to the CBI. The ruling government itself approached the court opposing the transfer of this case to the CBI. In the Anna University student case, even worse, the question of who that "Sir" is still remains unanswered. In Thanjavur, when a woman who was sexually assaulted went to file a complaint with the support of her family, the police made her travel several kilometers and took an entire day just to register the complaint. Every day, we only post hashtags saying Save her, Save her. But no one follows what happens in that case or how it progresses. Beyond posting hashtags, what more can ordinary citizens like us do? In the Delhi Nirbhaya case, one of the accused went to prison at the age of 17, came out at 18, and the government even provided him with a sewing machine for rehabilitation.

Have any of them ever thought about the number of problems faced by the victim? For a woman to recover from such trauma and return to her previous life takes years. Some undergo psychological counselling for many years due to mental stress. Some die by suicide. What wrong did they do to deserve that? In some cases, even their own families refuse to accept them,  and this too happens in this very country. Not all men commit such crimes, but in most instances, a man is the cause of such wrongdoing. A 5 year old child, a 3 month old infant… I simply do not understand. A few years ago, there was even a news report about a young man misbehaving with an elderly woman. These are children, what do perpetrators see in them that leads to such abuse? And in the case of an elderly woman… In nearly 90% of such cases, substance abuse is the root cause. A woman cannot walk alone on the road. She cannot wait at a bus stand after 9 PM. If she does, society witnesses daily how many people approach her inappropriately. This is not a problem that happens to someone else and can be ignored. Today it is that woman; tomorrow it could happen in our own home. Until a safe environment is created for women, there remains a constant fear of this society every single day.

I watched the film yesterday evening, but I felt it required a more detailed reflection, which is why I am recording this after careful thought. a decade back, in The Hindu, MP @KanimozhiDMK wrote an article beginning with Mahatma Gandhi’s quote: “An eye for an eye makes the whole world blind,” arguing that the death penalty is inhumane and unjust. She also referred to what Shibban Lal Saxena said against capital punishment. In the same article, she stated: “Some argue that the death penalty is the only way to deter heinous crime, especially violence against women and children. But a comprehensive study done last year in the United States found that there is no credible evidence that the death penalty has any deterrent effect on crime.” In other words, while some argue that the death penalty is the only solution to deter heinous crimes, particularly those against women and children, a study conducted in the United States found no credible evidence that capital punishment deters such crimes. Then what other punishment would reduce such crimes?

Crimes are continuing relentlessly, and the safety of women is becoming increasingly questionable. Even when information is sought through RTI, proper responses are not provided. Even when perpetrators are caught, they do not receive appropriate punishment. In such a situation, what other way is there to prevent these crimes? Will imprisoning offenders reduce sexual crimes against women and children? If execution does not reduce them, how will imprisonment alone make a difference? If the accused is a minor, special concessions are granted. I cannot see this merely as a film. We have all heard of the Pollachi sexual assault case. Some came to power after politically criticizing former minister Pollachi Jayaraman for allegedly helping to conceal the crime. But how many know that it was Pollachi Jayaraman who arranged legal assistance for the victim? When the police delayed registering the case, how many know that he stood by the victim and ensured that the case was filed immediately? A weekly magazine wrote whatever it wished, believing it was opposing the then ruling government. That is not wrong, but had they thought even a little about the victim’s pain at the time, they might have avoided certain words. It is not that a journalist with 40 years of experience did not know what to report and what to convey to the people. Crimes against women continue, and so do changes in government.

In Parliament, it was said that laws have been strengthened and punishments have been increased. Yet, somewhere in Tamilnadu, such incidents continue every single day. In the Anna University student case, there are still those who ask why the student came out at 8 PM? What necessity did she have to step out at that time? Someone even raised this question boldly in the public media debate, and to this day, no action has been taken against him. This is the law. If the law bends according to individuals, one is compelled to ask, "நாணல் போல வளைவதுதான் சட்டமாகுமா? அதை வளைப்பதற்கு வழக்கறிஞர் பட்டம் வேணுமா?" Acting in the Tamil remake of Anubhav Sinha’s Article 15 (Nenjuku Needhi) alone is not enough, those in power must take real steps to prevent such crimes. Why that has not happened remains unanswered. @taapsee @anubhavsinha @_gauravsolanki @kani_kusruti @revathyasha

Dear @raghav_chadha ,

I know you are doing very well in Parliament by raising small issues that were ignored by most Members of Parliament but have a bigger impact.

I am writing this post regarding an account lien and bank freeze by the Cyber Police of India.

In my case, the issue started when I received a message from my bank branch stating that my account had received a police notice of lien of 6000 rupees. I immediately went to my bank branch and asked them why my account had a lien of 6000 rupees. They followed some procedure and gave me a printout which contained the acknowledgement of my lien. One of the bank employees told me that I should contact the cyber police mentioned on the paper and provide them with the details of the 6000 rupees, such as where it came from and for what reason. However, they did not give me any specific reason why my bank account had received the lien.

Later, I checked my bank statement to find the details of the 6000 rupees transaction and noticed that my case was reported on 6 December 2025, and I had received a transaction of 6000 rupees on the same date. I remember that my neighbour had sent me this 6000 rupees and asked me to withdraw it from the ATM because he had an urgent situation as his mother was going to her village due to an emergency. As a friend, I withdrew the money and gave it to him.

Now I have all the proofs and details to explain to the police, so I emailed all the details to the Bangalore Cyber Cell or the police station where my notice was issued, as mentioned in the acknowledgement given by my bank. However, I did not receive any response. I then tried to contact the investigation officer mentioned in the report. I called several times, keeping a gap of five to six hours out of respect for his time and duties, as they may have many other responsibilities. I also sent him a message on WhatsApp, but there was still no response.

After four to five days, I called again, and this time he picked up the call. He was speaking in the local language, which I did not understand, as I am from Maharashtra and not familiar with the local language of Bangalore. I then started speaking in English, and he told me that I have to come to Bangalore and verify my documents. I explained that for 6000 rupees, it would not be beneficial for me to travel to Bangalore because transportation, food, and stay would cost more than 6000 rupees. He said that he does not know and that I have to come, otherwise he will not issue the No Objection Certificate, and then he ended the call.

This issue may look small, but similar issues are happening everywhere, and no one is noticing them. It feels like “Kare koi aur bhare koi.” Many innocent people face this issue, and it remains unresolved. Because of chain transactions that come into accounts, some people are unable to use their own money. If I travel, I will have to spend more than 6000 rupees to remove the lien. I believe this issue can be resolved through email or online verification, but the investigation officer denied it.

I am also tagging Pushpendra Sir @pushpendrakum and Bangalore Cyber Police @BlrCityPolice . If you could please look into this matter.

Thank you.

 In March 2026, ahead of the Kerala Assembly elections (polling on 9 April 2026), a 2019 Election Commission of India (ECI) letter redistributed by the Kerala Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office was found to carry the seal of the BJP’s Kerala unit. This sparked a political row, followed by police-directed efforts to remove related social media posts

This takedown action itself became controversial, with critics framing it as an attempt to suppress discussion of an official lapse during an election period, while authorities maintained it was necessary to stop the circulation of a withdrawn and erroneous document that was being used to question the ECI’s credibility.The episode remained a flashpoint in the final stretch of the Kerala campaign, with the ECI treating it as a corrected administrative mistake and the opposition presenting it as evidence of deeper concerns about the poll body’s independence.The letter and the seal
The document was an ECI communication dated 19 March 2019 containing guidelines/FAQs on the publicity of candidates’ criminal antecedents (following a Supreme Court judgment). CPI(M) and Congress shared versions online showing the BJP Kerala unit’s seal. It had been circulated by the Kerala CEO’s office to political parties, District Election Officers, and Returning Officers as part of clarifications around mid-March 2026.thesouthfirst.comKerala CEO / ECI explanation:
It was described as a “purely clerical error.” The BJP Kerala unit had approached the CEO’s office seeking clarification on the (by then revised) 2019 guidelines and submitted a photocopy of the original directive that already bore the party’s seal. Staff overlooked this and redistributed that version. The error was identified; on 21 March a formal withdrawal notice was issued telling recipients to disregard the document. An Assistant Section Officer was suspended pending inquiry. Later, a Deputy CEO and a Section Officer were relieved of election-related duties.livemint.comOpposition parties (CPI(M) and Congress) rejected the clerical-error account. They alleged compromised institutional neutrality, claiming seals were being “casually swapped” and questioning whether the ECI and BJP shared the same “power centre.” Some BJP responses labelled the circulation of the old document as misinformation or a political plot.thewire.inDeletion of posts controversyActing on an ECI directive (under the Model Code of Conduct), the Kerala Police cyber cell issued notices to X (Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, and numerous individual accounts. They demanded removal of posts sharing the letter that carried the BJP seal.  Police argued the content insulted the Election Commission, undermined its integrity and transparency, spread false claims about a rectified clerical error, and risked public order or communal harmony by potentially fuelling political division. 🚨 Binance P2P se Bank Account Freeze? Poori Guide + Real Solution (2026)

Bhai aur beheno, agar aap bhi Binance P2P trading karte ho aur suddenly bank account freeze ho gaya hai toh pareshan mat ho. Yeh bahut common problem hai India mein. Innocent log bhi fas jaate hain jab kisi buyer/seller ka paisa kisi fraud case se link hota hai.

Yeh steps follow karo - 

1️⃣ Sabse Pehle Bank Branch Jaao  
   - Freeze ka exact reason, Cyber Crime complaint number, IO naam aur Police Station details lo.  
   - Written notice maang lo.

2️⃣ Saare Proofs Collect Karo (Bahut Important)  
   - Binance P2P complete order history (screenshots)  
   - Buyer/Seller ke saath chat  
   - Payment proof (UPI, bank transfer screenshot)  
   - Bank statement jisme transaction dikhe  
   - Aadhaar, PAN, Binance account details

3️⃣ Binance Support ko turant contact karo  
   - App mein Help section → Submit ticket  
   - Order ID aur proofs attach karo. Woh counterparty ko investigate kar sakte hain.

4️⃣ Cyber Cell mein Representation Daalo  
   - Local Cyber Police Station ya online portal pe jaao.  
   - Detailed application likho ki transaction genuine tha Binance P2P pe hua.  
   - Saare proofs attach karo.  
   - Lawyer (Cyber crime specialist) ki madad le lo - yeh bahut kaam aata hai.

5️⃣ Follow-up karte raho  
   - Har 7-10 din mein bank aur cyber cell ko call/email karo.  
   - Partial release ke liye request kar sakte ho.

Extra Tips jo future mein bacha sakte hain:
• P2P ke liye alag dedicated bank account use karo (savings account mat use karo)
• Sirf verified buyers/sellers ke saath trade karo
• Video verification ya proper KYC maango
• Bahut bade amounts ek baar mein mat trade karo
• Binance P2P risky hai India mein, agar ho sake toh avoid karo
